checks.invariant: Every value placed in a docker run argument that a lower-trust party (the hunting agent, the audited tree) can influence stays one value: no separator, option or flag can be injected.
checks.result: Argv-level injection is closed: spawn uses an argument array with no shell (spawnExec :190); name, agent and check are regex-pinned (:263,:270-271); env names are NAME-shaped with credential-looking names refused and values pushed as separate argv items (:274-279,:140); the image must match PINNED (:35,:102) and probe runs `docker image inspect <image>` first, so an image string that docker would read as a flag fails the probe; command words come after the image (:141). The three --mount strings (:130,:133,:134) are different: they are built by template with raw paths, and Docker splits --mount values at commas into key=value fields. The only escaping is none. inputsDir is the realpath of an agent-named folder, checked only by containment in agents/<agent>/inputs (:285-293). Mask file paths come straight from walk() over the audited tree (:117; hunt-files.mjs:25-31 filters nothing by character) and are placed after `target=/target/`. A folder or file name holding `,source=` followed by nested folders turns the rest of the path into a second source= field. Which later field Docker keeps cannot be observed here.

checks.invariant: A control upstream of dockerArgs would stop a hunting agent from creating a comma-named inputs folder or passing it through --inputs.
checks.result: None found. During a hunt, writes are allowed anywhere under reviews/<id>/ with no name rule (hooks/qa-guardrail:904-912), and the arguments of the plugin's own hunt scripts are not judged (hooks/lib/qa-shell-writes.mjs:1233-1256). Nothing in runCheck rejects ',' or '"' in inputsDir (:283-294) or in mask paths (:327).

unresolved: Whether the installed Docker CLI keeps the later of two source= fields in one --mount value (outside source, needs a Docker engine)
The sandbox is unavailable for this run, so no docker command was run

checks.invariant: The container sees none of the project's key material, MCP secrets file, run records or review folders, and nothing secret-shaped it prints reaches the artifact.
checks.result: The mask set is sound for ordinary names: maskPaths masks reviews/ and .ultrapowers/ as read-only tmpfs, every file matching the shared KEY_RE (guard-paths.mjs:180, matched on the lowercased path, mounted by original-case name) plus .dev.vars, and .agents/mcp-secrets.env, each over an empty regular file the runner checks (:304-315). Symlinks are skipped by walk() but a container-side link cannot reach a host file. The container gets an empty environment, a credential-looking --env name is refused, and the redaction runs on the whole text before the 64 KiB cut (:345-348). The weakness is in the mask file path: it is the same unescaped `target=/target/${file}` text (:133) built from names the audited tree controls, so a hostile tree can inject a source= field and mount a host path over a decoy file. That is the same root cause as the inputs-folder variant and is consolidated under the one fingerprint. The redaction (:148-166) is the last layer and is weak in this setting: JSON-quoted `"apiKey": "value"` is not matched (the name must be followed directly by : or =); a private key printed without its END line is not matched; any encoding (base64, hex, reversal) passes. See hardening for the pathological-backtracking cost of the assignment pattern.

unresolved: Same blocker as the linked candidate: no Docker run is possible in this run, and the readability of a mounted host file for uid 65534 on a given host is outside source

checks.invariant: An artifact the verifier accepts is a regular file the runner wrote, at the path and with the content it logged; no path, link or component can redirect a read or write outside the run folder.
checks.result: The runner enforces this. parseRunRel restricts the run id and number (:232-240); reviewFolderProblem lstat-checks each step for links and compares realpaths (autopilot-lib.mjs:22-42); the artifacts folder is realpath-compared to the exact expected path before the container starts (:317-320); the artifact is created with flag wx, so an existing file or link is refused (:323,:360); the SHA-256 of the written bytes is appended to .ultrapowers/sandbox/<id>/run-<n>.jsonl, which the guardrail's MARKER_RE keeps from agents. verifyArtifact accepts only agents/<id>/artifacts/<name>.txt with plain repo and id (:381-383), refuses a link or non-regular file (regularFileProblem, autopilot-lib.mjs:48-54), takes the last log line for that (repo, artifact), and compares the current SHA-256 (:386-396). A forged log line, a rewritten artifact and a copy to another path each fail. A swap of the artifacts folder during the up-to-120-second container run needs a link, and the hunt's agents have only read verbs and a write tool that creates no link. hunt-verdict.mjs:316-327 calls verifyArtifact for every local check of every unit and attempt, and reports a failure as a problem.

checks.invariant: What verify proves is stated correctly: provenance of bytes, not truth of a claim.
checks.result: verify binds an artifact to the runner's write only. The artifact holds whatever the audited (hostile) code printed, so a printed `exploit succeeded` line proves nothing about the vulnerability, and a ledger can cite any verified artifact of the run for any claim. That is a property of the design; the verdict's other checks (hunt-verdict.mjs, owned by h4-verdict) are where the claim is judged. Recorded as hardening, not a finding.

candidates.title: Sandbox --mount strings take unescaped comma-bearing paths, so a path can inject a second source= field and bind a host path into the container
candidates.description: hunt-sandbox.mjs builds three --mount values by template: the repository (:130), each masked file (:133) and the agent's inputs folder (:134). Docker splits a --mount value at commas into key=value fields. Nothing rejects or quotes a comma, a double quote or a newline in the interpolated path. Variant A (the agent): a prompt-injected hunting agent writes files under reviews/<id>/run-<N>/<repo>/agents/<agent>/inputs/ in a folder tree such as `x,source=` / `<abs host path components>` and calls `hunt-sandbox.mjs run --inputs agents/<agent>/inputs/x,source=/<host path>`. The realpath containment check passes, and the argument becomes `type=bind,source=<real inputs>/x,source=/<host path>,target=/inputs,readonly`. If Docker keeps the later source=, the host path (the project root with `.env`, `.agents/mcp-secrets.env`, `.ultrapowers/runs`, or `/home/<user>`) is bind-mounted read-only at /inputs, outside every mask. The agent knows its own project root from its working directory. A command it chooses (for example `cat`, base64) then prints the content into the artifact; the redaction patterns catch only assignment-shaped and vendor-prefixed values, and the artifact is a committed file under reviews/. Variant B (the audited tree): maskPaths takes file names from walk() over the audited tree. A tree holding nested folders `a,source=` / `home` / `u` / `.ssh` and a file `id_rsa` (the whole path matches KEY_RE) plus a plain file `a` yields `target=/target/a,source=/home/u/.ssh/id_rsa`, which can bind a host file over the decoy for the hostile target code to read. A name such as `.env.x,y` yields an invalid field and makes docker fail (exit 125), so the sandbox is permanently refused for that tree. Boundary crossed: a lower-trust principal (the agent, or the audited tree whose code runs in the container) selects a host path mounted into a container, and the key-material mask and the guardrail's key-file read refusal do not apply to it. Source-level change that enforces the invariant: refuse any repoDir, inputsDir or mask path containing ',', '"', CR or LF (or CSV-quote the whole value) before building the --mount strings, and add a regression case for a folder named `x,source=` in --inputs and for a tree file `a,source=/etc/id_rsa`.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: Mount specifications are built by string interpolation of paths whose names a lower-trust party controls, and the comma that separates Docker's --mount fields is neither rejected nor quoted, so a path can add or replace fields such as source=.

trace.description: The agent's --inputs value (opts.inputs) and the audited tree's file names (through maskPaths) enter runCheck.
resolve(runRepoDir, inputsRel) is realpath'd and checked only for containment in agents/<agent>/inputs and for being a folder; a comma in any folder name is accepted.

walk(repoDir) returns every file path of the audited tree unfiltered; KEY_RE matches on `.ssh`, `id_rsa` or `.env` anywhere in the path, so a hostile name with a comma and a key-looking tail is kept in files.
inputsDir and masks go to dockerArgs with no check of ',' or '"'.
`--mount type=bind,source=${inputsDir},target=/inputs,readonly` (and the same shape for masked files at :133): the comma-joined string reaches the Docker CLI, which parses it as CSV fields.

evidence.description: The mask mount uses `target=/target/${file}` with a file name from the audited tree and no escaping.
walk() accepts every name from readdirSync, skipping only symlinks and a few folders; no character is filtered.
During a hunt, writes are allowed anywhere under reviews/<id>/ with no rule on name characters, so the agent can create the comma-named folder tree.
The arguments of the plugin's own hunt scripts are not judged, so the --inputs value passes the shell guardrail.
KEY_RE matches id_rsa, authorized_keys and `.ssh` as substrings of any path, which is what lets a decoy tree path with a comma pass as key material.
The last layer, redact(), is pattern-based; JSON-quoted names, truncated key blocks and any encoding of the content are not redacted.

blockers: The sandbox is unavailable for this run (no hunt.sandbox in .agents/ultrapowers.json), so no docker command can be run
Docker's handling of a repeated source= (and of a target path that is absent) in one --mount value is not source-visible and must be observed on the installed engine

Whether container uid 65534 can read a given host file or folder (a 600 file owned by the host user is unreadable on a Linux engine; Docker Desktop's file sharing differs) is a host fact outside source
On a Windows host the injected source would have to start with a backslash and cannot carry a drive letter, so the reachable case is a Linux or macOS host; this is not settled by source

validation_plan.local: With a Docker engine and a digest-pinned dummy image, create a dummy folder /tmp/h2probe holding marker.txt (no real secret). Create an inputs folder tree `agents/h2/inputs/x,source=/tmp/h2probe` (nested folders x,source= -> tmp -> h2probe) and call runCheck or the CLI with --inputs pointing at it and the command `ls /inputs`. Pass if the artifact lists marker.txt (the dummy host folder) and not the inputs folder content. Repeat for variant B with a tree file path `a,source=/tmp/h2probe/id_rsa` plus a plain file `a`, and run `ls -l /target/a`. Also run with a name such as `.env.x,y` and note the docker exit.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner confirms on the supported Docker versions and hosts (Linux, macOS Docker Desktop) that the later source= wins and that uid 65534 can read a world-readable host file such as a project .env mounted this way.

hardening: hunt-sandbox.mjs:158 ASSIGNMENT is an unanchored pattern with two adjacent open-ended character runs around the keyword alternation, run over up to 4 MiB of output the audited code controls (redact at :162, called at :348 before the cap). A long run of text like `key.key.key.` with no `=` should cause polynomial backtracking and hang the runner after the container has exited, so no artifact or log line is written. That is a local hunt stall, not a false pass, but the container's wall-clock limit does not cover it. Not run here. Fix: bound the name run (for example {0,64}) or scan line by line.

redact() misses JSON-style secrets (`"password": "x"`, `{"token":"x"}`), a private key block without its END line, quoted values with spaces, and any encoded form; it is defense in depth only and must not be the control for any content the container can reach beyond what the agent can already read.

The container mounts the whole repository including .git (MASK_SKIP, :40): .git/config can hold a remote URL with basic-auth credentials (`https://user:pass@host` is not redacted) and the full history. The agent can read the same files, so no new reader, but a clone with an embedded credential would reach the committed artifact. Consider masking .git/config.

KEY_RE does not match `.envrc`, `.htpasswd`, `credentials.json`, `*.tfvars` or `terraform.tfstate`, and the mask walk skips node_modules; the shared rule is peer-owned (h1-guardrail), noted here only because maskPaths depends on it.

--check names are not screened against Windows device names (RESERVED_AGENTS covers only --agent, :47,:270): `--check nul` writes nul.txt to the NUL device and verifyArtifact then refuses it as not a regular file. It fails closed, but the runner logs a hash for a file that was never stored.

hunt-sandbox.mjs verify and the ledger prove that the runner wrote an artifact, not that its text supports a claim; text printed by the audited code (including a spoofed `result:` or `--- stderr ---` line) lands in the artifact body after the header. Judges of the verdict should treat artifact bodies as hostile output.

The `image` string is passed to docker run as a bare argument (:141) and PINNED allows a leading `-` before the @sha256; the probe's `docker image inspect <image>` fails for such a value, which keeps it out, but only because the probe runs first; the config trust itself is peer-owned (h3-preflight).
